derivations.claim:
By [F11], pullbacks under $z$ of chart neighborhoods covering its image admit a finite subcover of $[a,b]$; refine it to a finite subdivision $a=t_0<\cdots<t_N=b$ such that each closed subsegment lies in one chart. Continuity of the given family lets us shrink its parameter interval so each family subsegment remains in that chart. Write chart coordinates $x_\epsilon^a(\tau)$, $J^a=\partial_\epsilon x_\epsilon^a|_0$, and $U^a=\partial_\tau x_0^a$. Differentiating the free-action integrand under the integral by [F6], and applying [F7]–[F9] to $Q=g_{ab}(x_\epsilon)\partial_\tau x_\epsilon^a\partial_\tau x_\epsilon^b$ at $Q=-c^2$, gives on each subsegment

$$\delta S_{\rm free}=m\int\left(g_{ab}(\partial_\tau J^a)U^b+\tfrac12(\partial_cg_{ab})J^cU^aU^b\right)d\tau.$$

The integrand is continuous, so [F15] makes it Riemann integrable.

The factors $J^a$ and $g_{ab}U^b$ are $C^1$, so their derivatives are continuous and integrable by [F15]. Integrating the $\partial_\tau J^a$ term of step 1.1 by parts with [F10], and using the Christoffel formula and metric compatibility of [F2], gives on each subsegment

$$\delta S_{\rm free}=m[g(J,U)]_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}-m\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}g(J,\nabla_UU)\,d\tau.$$

When the subsegment endpoints are fixed, the boundary term vanishes and this is the chart-local specialization of [F3]; at internal subdivision points we retain the displayed term.

On each chart subsegment, $A_a(z(\tau))$ and $J^a$ are $C^1$, so their derivatives are continuous and integrable by [F15]. Differentiating the interaction integrand by [F6]–[F8] gives $q\bigl((\partial_cA_a)J^cU^a+A_a\partial_\tau J^a\bigr)$. Integration by parts [F10] yields

$$\delta S_{\rm int}=q[A(J)]_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}+q\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}(\partial_cA_a-\partial_aA_c)J^cU^a\,d\tau=q[A(J)]_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}+q\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}F_{ca}J^cU^a\,d\tau,$$

with the component ordering fixed by [F4].

Sum steps 1.2 and 1.3 over the finite subdivision. At each internal cut, the free boundary scalar $g(J,U)$ and the interaction boundary scalar $A(J)$ agree in the adjacent charts, so their endpoint terms cancel. At $a,b$ they vanish because $J(a)=J(b)=0$. Repeated use of [F16] sums the remaining integrals to the stated first-variation formula.

Let $C_a:=-m(\nabla_UU)_a+qF_{ab}U^b$ be the continuous coefficient from steps 1.2–1.4. If $C_{a_0}(\tau_0)\ne0$ at an interior point, continuity gives a chart subinterval $I$ on which it has constant sign and magnitude at least $d>0$; choose a nondegenerate compact interval $K=[\tau_-,\tau_+]\subset I$. Define $\sigma=1$ when $C_{a_0}(\tau_0)>0$ and $\sigma=-1$ when $C_{a_0}(\tau_0)<0$. Use [F5] to choose a cutoff $0\le\chi\le1$ equal to $1$ on $K$ and supported in $I$, and set the $a_0$ coordinate of a variation field to $\sigma\chi$ and its other components to zero. On its compact support, $-g(U,U)=c^2$ and $-g(U,N)>0$ have positive minima by [F13] and [F14]. The chart displacement $x(z_\epsilon)=x(z)+\epsilon J^{\rm ch}$, extended by $z_\epsilon=z$ outside the support, therefore stays in $O$ and remains future timelike for sufficiently small $|\epsilon|$, by continuity and compactness.

On $I$, the function $f(\tau)=\sigma C_{a_0}(\tau)\chi(\tau)$ is nonnegative, and on $K$ it is at least $d$. It is continuous and hence integrable by [F15]; [F12] gives $\int_{\tau_-}^{\tau_+} f\,d\tau\ge d(\tau_+-\tau_-)>0$. Repeated use of [F16] and nonnegativity on the two remaining parts of $I$ shows $\int_I f\,d\tau\ge\int_K f\,d\tau$; the variation vanishes outside $I$. Thus step 1.4 gives $\delta S>0$, contradicting stationarity. Therefore stationarity for every local chart-supported variation forces $C_a=0$ in the interior and, by continuity, at the endpoints. Conversely, $C_a=0$ makes step 1.4 vanish for every admissible variation; raising the covector index with the nondegenerate metric gives $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$.

derivations.claim: Choose a chart $(U,\varphi)$ with $x_0\in U\subseteq O$ and write its coordinates as $y^a=\varphi^a(x)$. The state domain $\varphi(U)\times\mathbb R^4$ is open and the equation is $\dot y^a=U^a$, $\dot U^a=-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(y)U^bU^c+(q/m)F^a{}_b(y)U^b$, where $F^a{}_b:=g^{ac}F_{cb}$ by the definition of $F^\sharp$. Its right-hand side is $C^1$ because $g$ and $\Gamma$ are smooth and $F$ is $C^1$, using the sum, product and composition rules [F5, F6]. Choose a closed convex coordinate box about $(\varphi(x_0),U_0^a)$ contained in that state domain. It is compact by [F9], so each continuous first partial derivative of the vector field is bounded by [F8]. Along the segment between any two states, the one-variable mean value theorem [F4], applied to each component, bounds the difference of vector-field values by a constant times the state difference. Thus the field is locally Lipschitz.

Apply [F3] to this locally Lipschitz coordinate vector field to obtain a unique local solution. Because the vector field is $C^1$, composing it with the $C^1$ solution and applying [F6] shows its derivative is $C^1$, so the curve is $C^2$. The coordinate equation is equivalent to the covariant equation by the Christoffel coefficients of [F2], so the local chart solutions agree under chart changes and share the asserted uniqueness.

Metric compatibility and antisymmetry give $\frac{d}{d\tau}g(U,U)=2g(U,\nabla_UU)=2(q/m)g(U,F^\sharp(U))=2(q/m)F(U,U)=0$. Thus the initial norm $-c^2$ is preserved. Let $N$ be the smooth timelike field defining the time orientation. Since each solution value $U$ is timelike, [F7] gives $g(U,N)\neq0$; this continuous function therefore keeps its initially negative sign on the connected local interval, so $U$ remains future directed.
